pages.text: A banquet begins with the table. Dishes go on the table top, or right up against its side.$(br2)Both the quality and the variety of your dishes raise the spread's appeal. Put them where they can be reached, or a guest may end up eating on the tabletop.

A spread with nowhere to sit is not a banquet. Tables and chairs within three blocks of one another all count as the same banquet. Spacing them out helps guests move about and take food, though not too far.$(br2)Hold the banquet in an open place, where guests can easily reach it.

A letter names nobody. Right-click the table with one and the note goes out to Gensokyo at large, to everyone who might conceivably come. A letter is spent on the send.$(br2)Only one banquet may be under way in an area at a time, so wait for the last guest to leave before you send another.
